definition.description:
A general software change, from plan to release: plan, review the plan,
implement, verify, review the change, release.

For: changes to any codebase. A person approves the plan and the release,
and confirms abandoning the work. A review with a blocking finding, or a
failed verify, sends the work back. Every check and the release are bound
to the commit named in change-summary. Stages name tracker status keys, so
a work item can drive a ticket; drop the stages' tracker blocks if it will
not. For a swamp extension, build-swamp-extension.yaml adds a quality score
and a manifest version check.

Change first: verify's command (your project's checks), the skills the
plan-review and code-review stages load, and release's description (how
your project ships).

work.systemPrompt:
First, check the work is not a duplicate of another ticket. If it
is, find out whether that ticket, the primary, already has a work
item: run the tracker's claim on it with dryRun=true, which writes
nothing. Record duplicate-of with the primary's stable id, its
display id and why, and wait for a person to approve
duplicate-confirmation; do not plan. Once it is approved, move the
work to the primary. When the primary has no work item, retarget
this work item onto the primary's externalRefs and publish at once,
so the ticket index follows before anyone claims the primary, then
plan the primary's work here. When it has one, take the duplicate
exit.

Plan the change with the person. Read the code it touches first.
Record plan with a summary, the steps in order (each naming the files
it touches) and the testing strategy.

On a later plan, read the injected plan (the last one), plan-review
(its review) and plan-feedback (the person's latest feedback); the
first plan has none of them. After a review sends the plan back,
address its findings. After revise, address the feedback. Record
feedbackIncorporated as the last plan's list, adding the feedback word
for word unless it is already the list's last entry: after rework,
plan-feedback is the feedback the last plan already answered.

feedbackIncorporated.description: Every round of a person's plan feedback this plan answers, oldest first.

transitions.name: duplicate
transitions.description: The work duplicates a primary ticket that already has a work item; a person confirms it. When the primary has none, the work item is retargeted onto it instead, and the cel gate closes this exit to it. "builtin" there is the built-in tracker's externalRefs key; a definition for Linear names "linear".

config.message: this work item is on the primary ticket now; plan it here

stages.description: Adversarial review of the current plan. Open blocking findings send it back; none lets it through. With nothing blocking, approving carries the open medium and low findings into implement, which receives plan-review; revise is for when the person wants the plan itself changed and reviewed again.

work.systemPrompt:
You are an adversarial reviewer. Try to refute this plan:
{{planSummary}}
Check its steps against the code and its testing strategy against the
risks.
Rate a finding critical or high only if the plan would ship a
defect, lose data, break a stated rule, or make the declared checks
meaningless. Gaps in process, logistics or manual verification that
the automated checks already cover are medium at most. Judge the
plan against the size of the change: do not ask for verification
machinery bigger than the change, and give the smallest adequate fix
for each finding. Report findings with severities, and do not soften
the severity of a real defect.

evidence.name: plan-feedback
evidence.description: A person's feedback on the plan, in their words; revise needs it. The round is the cycle it was recorded in.

transitions.name: rework
transitions.description: The fresh plan review has an open critical or high finding, so the plan goes back to be fixed.

transitions.name: revise
transitions.description: A person sent the plan back without a blocking finding, to change the plan itself and have it reviewed again. To act on non-blocking findings during implement, approve instead. Manual, so it never fires on its own, and the person's feedback is recorded first, so every revision carries its reason to the next plan.

gates.description: The person's feedback on this plan is recorded.

stages.description: Implement the plan and commit it.

work.systemPrompt:
Implement the plan. Commit the work, then record change-summary with
the full 40-character SHA of the commit to check and review. Do not
open a pull request. After a check or review sends the work back, fix
it, commit, and record change-summary again for the new commit.

stages.description: Run the checks on the change-summary commit and record checks, with one result per check.

work.systemPrompt:
Check out commit {{commit}} and run the stage's command. Record checks
with that commit, the overall status, and one result per check (its
name, status and, when it failed, the output that shows why). Record
only what you ran and saw.
work.command: the project's format, lint, type and test checks (replace this with the real commands)

schema.$comment: An overall pass cannot contain a failed result.

config.message: checks must be for the change-summary commit

transitions.name: failed
transitions.description: The checks failed, so the change goes back to be fixed.

stages.description: Adversarial review of the change. Open blocking findings send it back; none lets it through.

work.systemPrompt:
You are an adversarial reviewer. Review commit {{commit}}:
{{changeSummary}}
Check it against the plan.
Rate a finding critical or high only if the change would ship a
defect, lose data, break a stated rule, or make the declared checks
meaningless. Gaps in process, logistics or manual verification that
the automated checks already cover are medium at most. Judge the
change against the size of the change: do not ask for verification
machinery bigger than the change, and give the smallest adequate fix
for each finding. Report findings with severities, and do not soften
the severity of a real defect.

transitions.name: rework
transitions.description: The fresh code review has an open critical or high finding, so the change goes back to be fixed.

transitions.name: revise
transitions.description: A person sent the change back without a blocking finding. Manual, so it never fires on its own.

work.systemPrompt:
Release the reviewed commit, and record release with the commit that
shipped and where.

transitions.name: rework
transitions.description: The release was blocked; go back and change the work.

stages.description: The work duplicated a primary ticket that has its own work item.

scenarios.description: A person declines the plan without a blocking finding and sends it back with feedback. revise is refused until the feedback is recorded, and the next plan lists the feedback it answers.

steps.note: The person wants the plan split before any code is written

payload.feedback: Split the list method from the pagination change

feedbackIncorporated: Split the list method from the pagination change

scenarios.description: A change walks from plan to done through the real gates, with a rework round from each review and from verify. A high plan finding sends the plan back and holds approval; a low one blocks nothing; a failed check and a critical code-review finding each send the work back to implement; checks for another commit do not count.

expect.refused: no unresolved finding at a blocking severity

steps.note: Checks for another commit do not count

expect.refused: checks must be for the change-summary commit

scenarios.description: The ticket duplicates a primary that already has a work item. The agent records duplicate-of, a person approves, and the work item ends at duplicate; publish marks the ticket a duplicate and closes it.
The primary had no work item, so the work item was retargeted onto it. The approved gate no longer ends it: the duplicate exit is closed on the primary, and the work is planned there.

definition.description: The factory definition: its stages, transitions, gates and prompts. Start from one of the skill's examples.

tracker.description: The tracker instance work items publish to, e.g. board: a model of the type the definition's tracker kind needs (the built-in tracker, @swamp/stagecraft/tracker, unless it names another)

scenarios.description: Saved scenarios: work items walked through the definition, which validate runs

methods.name: validate
methods.description: Check the definition in full, analyse it as a graph, and report every problem with its path
